references.text: The first time the Lord's angel calls to Abraham from heaven to stop the sacrifice of Isaac. Verse 15 marks the second time the angel calls.
The content of the angel's second message: God swears by himself and renews the promises to Abraham of blessing and numerous descendants because of his obedience.
The beginning of the trial where God asks Abraham to sacrifice his son Isaac, culminating in the angel's intervention and God's renewed promises.
God repeats to Isaac the promises he gave Abraham with an oath (cf. 22:16-18), pointing to Abraham's obedience as the basis for the blessing.
The psalmist reminds us of God's covenant with Abraham, which is directly related to the promises confirmed by oath in Genesis 22:15-18.
Hebrews reflects on Abraham's faith when he was tested with Isaac and understands the event in light of the hope of resurrection.
Hebrews refers directly to God swearing by himself when giving the promise to Abraham, which connects to the angel's message in Genesis 22:15-18.
Typological parallel: The angel who gives strength in the ultimate trial for Abraham and Jesus respectively.
